messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — ran a focused perf sweep across H100 and A100 for the new 30B model. Comparing our Triton custom kernels, FlashAttention variants, and the vendor fused-attention. Results are odd for long seqs, sharing raw numbers.
Maria: awesome, drop the numbers and config?
Sam: p50/p95 latency (ms) for seq=512 / batch=8 / beam=1:
```
H100 FlashV3: 21.3 / 45.8
H100 Triton-attn: 23.9 / 58.2
A100 FlashV3: 26.7 / 71.1
A100 Triton-attn: 24.5 / 62.9
Vendor-fused: 20.9 / 80.5
```
Sam: throughput (tokens/s) same run: H100 FlashV3 ~ 14.8k, Triton ~13.2k, A100 FlashV3 ~11.0k
AJ: where did q8/q4 quantization land?
Sam: we tested q8_0 and q4f16 on a separate pass. Q8 on H100 + FlashV3 gave 1.9x token/s vs fp16, but p95 tail widened by ~12ms. Q4 reduced mem but bumped p95 by ~35-40ms for seq 2048.
Liam: interesting — so FlashV3 wins for steady throughput, but tails on vendor-fused and q4 are worse for long seqs?
Sam: yup. For seq=2048 / batch=2:
```
H100 FlashV3: p50 88ms / p95 220ms / tokens/s 3.2k
H100 Triton: p50 95ms / p95 310ms / tokens/s 2.9k
A100 FlashV3: p50 120ms / p95 430ms / tokens/s 2.1k
Vendor-fused: p50 85ms / p95 520ms / tokens/s 3.0k
```
Maria: vendor-fused has low p50 but huge p95 on long seqs — does that correlate with memcpy spikes? any flamegraphs?
Sam: checked kernels on perf counters — vendor path triggers extra host<->device copies for kv reorg at large seq lengths. FlashV3 keeps kv layout on-GPU, hence steadier tail. Triton kernel has occasional grid-launch jitter when sequence length crosses tile boundaries.
AJ: what's latency SLO we care about here? 200ms p95?
Maria: product wants p95 < 300ms for interactive endpoints. For async batch endpoints we can accept higher.
Liam: so operational rule could be: route seq <=1024 to FlashV3 on H100, seq 1025-2048 to Triton on H100/A100 with larger batch, and seq>2048 avoid q4. But cost matters — FlashV3 on H100 is ~1.6x cost vs Triton on A100 in our price model.
Sam: proposed routing config (proto):
```
route_rules:
  - if: model == "30B" and seq <= 1024 and region == "us-west-2"
    kernel: flash_v3
    device_preference: [h100, a100]
  - if: seq > 1024 and seq <= 2048
    kernel: triton_custom
    device_preference: [h100, a100]
  - if: seq > 2048
    kernel: vendor_fused
    fallback: triton_custom
    quantization: avoid_q4
```
Maria: do we need region-specific knobs? I saw us-west-2 H100 p95 slightly worse than eu-west-1 H100 in the same test — likely noisy neighbors.
Sam: yes, region variance ~5-12% across runs. We should have a dynamic per-region calibration step during rollout. ops-bot: calibration job scheduled for us-west-2 at 03:00 UTC (job id: calib-1769123467).
AJ: For canary rollout rules, I'd add a safety margin: prefer Triton when p95 delta between flash_v3 and triton < 10% to save cost. Also auto-fallback if tail increases by >20% over baseline.
Liam: also track token-cost per request — FlashV3 on H100 reduces cost/token when throughput high, but spikes mean tail SLO violations costing support noise. Need to include support cost factors.
Sam: agree. Next steps: run auto-calibration job across regions + quantization sweep with seq buckets [256,512,1024,2048] and collect p50/p95/p99 + OOMs. I'll upload full CSV to the bench bucket.
Maria: thanks — can you paste the bench command you used?
Sam: sure:
```
./bench_runner --model 30B --kernels flash_v3,triton,vendor --devices h100,a100 --seq_lengths 256,512,1024,2048 --batch_sizes 1,2,4,8 --quant q8_0,q4f16,fp16 --out bench-1769123456.csv
```
AJ: ping me when CSV is uploaded; I'll sketch routing lambda for the control plane.
Liam: I'll add a Grafana dashboard panel for tail heatmap by region+kernel.
Sam: uploaded: s3://redwood-bench/eng-ml/1769123456/bench-1769123456.csv
Maria: perfect. ops-bot: create rollout ticket?
ops-bot: Created ticket #INF-8821: "kernel routing experiment + calibration" assigned to @Sam, @AJ, due 2026-04-02.
Sam: sweet. TL;DR: FlashV3 preferred for short/mid seq on H100 for best tokens/s; Triton is a cost-efficient fallback for many workloads; vendor-fused can give great p50 but terrible p95 for long sequences due to KV reorgs. We'll codify routing + dynamic calibration. :rocket:
